tool_arguments.query: NVIDIA Data Center revenue fiscal 2027 Q1 quarter ending April 2026 growth drivers

events.content: NVIDIA Data Center revenue fiscal 2027 Q1 quarter ending April 2026 growth drivers

NVIDIA’s Data Center revenue in **Q1 fiscal 2027 (quarter ended April 26, 2026)** was a record **$75.246 billion**, increasing **21% sequentially** from $62.314 billion in Q4 FY2026 and **92% year over year** from $39.112 billion in Q1 FY2026. [[1]]

**Principal growth drivers:** 
- The principal product catalyst was the continuing ramp of **Blackwell 300** systems. [[1]]
- Networking demand was also a major contributor, specifically for **InfiniBand, Spectrum-X Ethernet, and NVLink** solutions. [[1]]
- By legacy product grouping, Data Center **compute** revenue reached **$60.4 billion**—up **18% sequentially** and **77% year over year**—while Data Center **networking** revenue reached **$14.8 billion**, up **35% sequentially** and **199% year over year**. [[1]]
- Customer demand was broad: hyperscalers accounted for roughly **50%** of Data Center revenue and grew sequentially, while the other approximately 50% came from increasingly diversified buyers, including **AI clouds, industrial, enterprise, and sovereign-AI customers**. [[1]] 

In short, the 92% annual growth was not solely an accelerator-volume story: it reflected the Blackwell 300 ramp plus rapidly expanding high-performance networking attach, supported by both hyperscale deployments and a widening non-hyperscale AI-infrastructure customer base. [[1]]

Sources:
[S4.1] CFO Commentary on First Quarter Fiscal 2027 Results — https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27cfocommentary.htm

source_references.title: CFO Commentary on First Quarter Fiscal 2027 Results

tool_arguments.query: NVIDIA Data Center revenue fiscal 2026 Q4 quarter ending January 2026 growth drivers

events.content: NVIDIA Data Center revenue fiscal 2026 Q4 quarter ending January 2026 growth drivers

**NVIDIA Data Center revenue — Q4 FY2026 (quarter ended January 25, 2026):** **$62.3 billion**, a record, rising **22% sequentially** from Q3 FY2026 and **75% year over year** from Q4 FY2025. [[1]]

**Growth drivers**

- **Rapid AI-compute investment and agentic-AI adoption:** NVIDIA attributed demand to an “agentic AI inflection point,” with enterprises accelerating adoption of AI agents and customers investing heavily in AI-compute infrastructure. [[1]]
- **Grace Blackwell systems and NVLink:** Management highlighted Grace Blackwell with NVLink as a leading inference platform, citing substantially lower cost per token, which supports both inference deployment economics and customer demand for accelerated systems. [[1]]
- **Hyperscaler and cloud deployment:** AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure were identified as early planned deployers of the next-generation Vera Rubin-based instances, illustrating continued large-cloud demand for NVIDIA data-center platforms. [[1]]
- **Blackwell/Blackwell Ultra performance economics:** NVIDIA stated that Blackwell Ultra provided up to 50x better performance and 35x lower agentic-AI cost versus Hopper in a cited benchmark, strengthening the upgrade case for new AI infrastructure. [[1]]
- **Expanding customer ecosystem and infrastructure content:** NVIDIA announced a multiyear Meta partnership involving large-scale deployments of CPUs, networking, and millions of Blackwell and Rubin GPUs, while Meta also adopted Spectrum-X Ethernet across its infrastructure footprint. [[2]]
- **Inference-provider adoption:** NVIDIA said inference providers including Baseten, DeepInfra, Fireworks AI, and Together AI achieved AI-cost reductions of up to 10x using open-source models on Blackwell, supporting demand beyond the largest cloud platforms. [[1]]

**Bottom line:** Q4 Data Center growth was principally a Blackwell-led AI-infrastructure cycle, supported by hyperscaler/enterprise spending, the shift from training toward high-volume inference and agentic workloads, and the economics of NVIDIA’s integrated GPU, interconnect, CPU, and networking platform. [[1]] [[2]]

Sources:
[S5.1] NVIDIA Corporation - NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2026 — https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-2026/default.aspx

tool_arguments.query: NVIDIA Data Center revenue fiscal 2026 Q3 quarter ending October 2025 growth drivers

events.content: NVIDIA Data Center revenue fiscal 2026 Q3 quarter ending October 2025 growth drivers

**NVIDIA Data Center revenue — Q3 fiscal 2026 (quarter ended October 26, 2025):** **$51.2 billion** (reported as $51.215 billion), a quarterly record. It increased **25% sequentially** from Q2 FY2026 and **66% year over year** versus Q3 FY2025. [[1]]

**Primary growth drivers**

- **Accelerating AI-infrastructure demand:** NVIDIA characterized demand for AI computing as continuing to accelerate, supporting data-center spending by cloud providers, AI model developers, enterprises, and sovereign AI projects. [[2]]
- **Blackwell platform ramp:** The expansion was led by adoption of Blackwell-based systems, with GB300 shipments exceeding GB200 shipments and GB300 representing roughly two-thirds of Blackwell revenue, according to management commentary reported by Futurum. [[2]]
- **Networking attach and scale-out AI systems:** Data-center networking revenue reached **$8.2 billion**, up **162% year over year**, aided by NVLink scale-up systems, Spectrum-X Ethernet, and Quantum-X InfiniBand demand. [[2]]
- **System-level performance and efficiency:** NVIDIA highlighted Blackwell’s InferenceMAX benchmark results, including claimed **10x throughput per megawatt** relative to the prior generation, a performance-per-power proposition that supports AI-factory deployments. [[1]]
- **Large customer infrastructure commitments:** Announced commitments included OpenAI’s planned deployment of at least **10 gigawatts** of NVIDIA systems and Anthropic’s initial adoption of **1 gigawatt** of Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin capacity. These announcements underscore the breadth of demand, although they should not be interpreted as Q3 revenue booked in full. [[3]] [[1]] 

For context, NVIDIA’s consolidated Q3 FY2026 revenue was **$57.0 billion**, up **22% sequentially** and **62% year over year**, meaning Data Center accounted for roughly **90%** of company revenue in the quarter. [[4]] [[1]]

tool_arguments.query: NVIDIA Data Center revenue fiscal 2025 Q4 quarter ending October 2024 growth drivers

events.content: NVIDIA Data Center revenue fiscal 2025 Q4 quarter ending October 2024 growth drivers

NVIDIA’s quarter ending **October 27, 2024** was **Q3 of fiscal 2025**, not fiscal-Q4; it reported **Data Center revenue of $30.771 billion**, up **17% sequentially** from $26.272 billion and **112% year over year** from $14.514 billion. [[1]] [[2]] 

That represents sequential growth of about **$4.499 billion** and year-over-year growth of about **$16.257 billion**. [[2]]

**Principal growth drivers** were: 
- Demand for the **Hopper computing platform** to train and infer large-language models, recommendation engines, and other generative-AI applications. [[3]]
- Stronger Data Center **compute** sales—$27.6 billion, up **22% QoQ** and **132% YoY**—including significant growth in the H200 offering. [[3]]
- Demand across customer groups: cloud service providers contributed approximately **50%** of Data Center revenue, with the balance from consumer-internet and enterprise companies. [[3]]
- Broad compute and networking demand, including AI Ethernet/Spectrum-X, InfiniBand and Ethernet switches, SmartNICs, and BlueField DPUs. [[3]]
- Expanding cloud availability of Hopper H200 instances, including at AWS, CoreWeave, and Microsoft Azure. [[4]] 

For clarity, NVIDIA’s actual **Q4 FY2025** ended **January 26, 2025**, when Data Center revenue reached **$35.6 billion**, up 16% QoQ and 93% YoY. [[5]]

- Demand across customer groups: cloud service providers contributed approximately **50%** of Data Center revenue, with the balance from consumer-internet and enterprise companies. [[3]]
- Broad compute and networking demand, including AI Ethernet/Spectrum-X, InfiniBand and Ethernet switches, SmartNICs, and BlueField DPUs. [[3]]
- Expanding cloud availability of Hopper H200 instances, including at AWS, CoreWeave, and Microsoft Azure. [[4]] 

For clarity, NVIDIA’s actual **Q4 FY2025** ended **January 26, 2025**, when Data Center revenue reached **$35.6 billion**, up 16% QoQ and 93% YoY. [[5]]
